Case_17024/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Figure 2: Photograph of fluorescein stained left eye under blue light on day 30 of presentation. This adds contrast and helps delineate the full extent of corneal ulceration.

description.short_caption: Fluorescein-stained left eye under blue light showing corneal ulceration.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a fluorescein-stained left eye viewed under blue light. The fluorescein highlights a central corneal ulceration, which appears as a bright green area surrounded by a darker corneal background. The ulceration is irregular in shape, with well-demarcated edges. The blue light enhances the contrast, making the extent of the lesion more apparent.
visible_findings: irregular lesion with bright green fluorescence

Case_17024/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Figure 3: Photograph of left eye taken on day 40 of presentation. Rapid progression seen with complete opacification of the cornea suggestive of progressive keratitis

description.short_caption: Clinical photograph showing complete corneal opacification in the left eye, consistent with advanced keratitis.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph depicts the left eye with marked findings. The cornea is completely opacified, with a dense white appearance obscuring the underlying structures. The surrounding conjunctiva is erythematous and inflamed, indicative of significant irritation or infection. The findings are consistent with progressive keratitis, potentially infectious in etiology. The image highlights the advanced stage of the condition.
visible_findings: dense white appearance of the cornea

Case_17024/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Figure 4: SAB plate with a powdery white mold on day 5 of culture

description.short_caption: SAB plate showing a powdery white mold colony on day 5 of culture.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Sabouraud dextrose agar (SAB) plate with a mold colony exhibiting a powdery white surface. The colony appears circular with a slightly raised center and radiating folds or ridges. The texture suggests a filamentous fungal growth, consistent with mold. The image is taken at close range, emphasizing the colony morphology.

Case_17024/figure5.jpg.source_caption: Figure 5: Photograph of left eye on day 41 after presentation (1 day after his first corneal transplant)

description.short_caption: Photograph of left eye showing corneal transplant with sutures and signs of inflammation.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a close-up view of the left eye. The cornea has visible sutures consistent with a recent corneal transplant. The central corneal area appears hazy with a greenish discoloration, possibly indicating edema or infection. Surrounding conjunctiva is erythematous, suggesting inflammation. The eyelashes have yellow crusting, which may represent discharge or debris.
visible_findings: central corneal haze with green discoloration

Case_17024/figure6.jpg.source_caption: Figure 6: Photograph of left eye 54 days from presentation and 14 days post his first corneal transplant. Recurrence of an infiltrate at the inferior aspect of the temporary corneal graft.

description.short_caption: Photograph of left eye showing recurrence of an infiltrate at the inferior aspect of a corneal graft.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows a close-up view of the left eye. A temporary corneal graft is visible, secured with multiple sutures around its circumference. There is a hazy, white infiltrate at the inferior aspect of the graft, suggesting recurrence of infection or inflammation. The central corneal area appears relatively clear, but the peripheral infiltrate is prominent. The image was taken 14 days post-corneal transplant.
visible_findings: hazy white infiltrate at the inferior aspect of the graft

Case_17024/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Figure 1: Photograph of fluorescein stained left eye on day 30 of presentation demonstrated a central infiltrate and the extent of corneal ulceration.

description.short_caption: Fluorescein-stained left eye showing a central corneal infiltrate and ulceration.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph depicts a close-up view of the left eye with fluorescein staining. A central greenish-yellow area is visible, consistent with a corneal infiltrate and ulceration. Surrounding conjunctival injection is evident, with prominent redness of the sclera. The fluorescein highlights the extent of the corneal defect, indicating significant involvement of the central cornea. The image suggests an advanced infectious process, possibly microbial keratitis.
